hook_text: One mosquito bite. Two weeks of fever. A lost harvest, and a daughter who misses school. That is how poverty spreads.
clip_script: A farmer gets malaria. She cannot work, her daughter stays home to nurse her, and the planting season passes. Multiply that by millions and you see why health shapes development. Now picture a ladder. Each extra year of good schooling helps a person earn more. When girls climb that ladder, their children are healthier and more likely to go to school too. But the steps must be strong. Years in a classroom are not enough if children never learn to read. And picture a house where everyone is fighting. Nothing gets built. War and corruption wreck schools and clinics. In 1966, Botswana was one of the poorest countries on earth. It found diamonds, kept the peace, held fair elections and spent the money on roads and schools. Health, learning and peace hold each other up. Break one, and the others wobble.
visual_style: A mosquito on an arm; a girl at a bedside with a school bag on the floor; a ladder with numbered steps; a map of Southern Africa highlighting Botswana with a diamond icon; three tent poles holding up a canvas.
pacing: Gentle opening, steady middle, uplifting close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to see how health, education and political stability shape development.
